meaning.en: To accept criticism, punishment or other unpleasant consequences for something you have done, instead of avoiding responsibility.
meaning.zh: 為自己做過的錯事承擔後果，接受批評、責罵、處分或其他不愉快結果，而不是逃避責任。

register.summaryEn: In this exercise, face the music is treated as informal to neutral.
register.summaryZh: 本練習把 face the music 視為非正式至中性的表達。

朋友或同事之間的勸告。
register.formalEn: The expression often carries a serious, firm or critical tone. In highly formal legal, disciplinary or official writing, expressions such as accept responsibility, accept the consequences or be held responsible may be more suitable.
register.formalZh: 這個表達通常帶有認真、堅定或批評的語氣。 在非常正式的法律、紀律或官方文件中，使用 accept responsibility、accept the consequences 或 be held responsible 可能更合適。

benefits.en: The idiom shows that somebody is no longer avoiding the result of their actions.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語表示某人不再逃避自己行為所帶來的結果。

benefits.en: She must face the music for what she did.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語可以把「接受批評、處分及責任」濃縮成一個簡潔表達。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful When Somebody Has Been Avoiding a Problem
benefits.titleZh: 適合說明某人一直逃避問題
benefits.en: Sooner or later, he will have to face the music.

benefits.titleZh: 可以用來提出堅定勸告
benefits.en: You should stop making excuses and face the music.
benefits.zh: 你應停止找藉口，承擔應有後果。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful in Stories and Conversations
benefits.en: Writers and speakers can use it at the point when a character must finally accept responsibility.
benefits.zh: 說故事或對話時，可以在人物終於需要承擔責任的一刻使用這個慣用語。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Not Automatically Better Than Plain English

history.en: The earliest currently identified printed example appeared in the New-Hampshire Statesman and State Journal on 2 August 1834. The writer demanded that another newspaper editor stop avoiding a serious question and accept responsibility. Other examples appeared in New Hampshire shortly afterwards, showing that the expression was already being used figuratively in the United States during the 1830s.
history.zh: 目前找到的最早印刷用例，出現在1834年8月2日的《New-Hampshire Statesman and State Journal》。 文中要求另一名報章編輯不要再逃避一項嚴重問題，並承擔責任。 其後不久，新罕布什爾州亦出現其他用例，顯示這個表達在十九世紀三十年代的美國已具有比喻意思。

history.en: Today, face the music means accepting criticism, punishment or responsibility for something one has done.
history.zh: 今天，face the music 表示為自己所做的事情承擔責任，接受批評、處分或其他後果。

origin.memoryEn: Do not turn away from the unpleasant “music”; turn towards it and accept what follows.
origin.memoryZh: 不要轉身逃避令人不快的「音樂」；要面對它，並接受隨之而來的後果。

questions.answer: The parents believe the teenagers should face the music for damaging the park.
questions.answerZh: 家長認為那些青少年應為破壞公園承擔後果。
